message.content:
Review: The design is closely aligned with the research question and substantially improves on what the aggregate export can establish. Its randomized coupling intervention, independent repeated runs, blocked condition order, fixed drive and disorder, synchronized measurements, and explicit distinction between the intervention’s causal effect and mediation through coarsening provide a credible basis for testing whether coupling changes temporal-order onset. The primary high-versus-low contrast and restricted-mean onset-time estimand are clearly specified, and censoring, pilot separation, threshold calibration, and the staged drive control are addressed thoughtfully.

Feedback: The main remaining validity risks are operational and analytical. First, pilot-selected coupling levels are chosen partly to produce distinct coarsening rates, so the confirmatory study should demonstrate that this separation replicates; otherwise, a null onset result may simply reflect a weak manipulation. Second, the proposed run-level false-positive calibration needs to match the complete onset procedure, including overlapping windows, consecutive-window persistence, and the full observation interval. Surrogates should be justified against plausible non-crystalline signals, since an inadequate null could misclassify onset. Third, specify the survival-model assumptions and the exact restricted-mean estimator, including how block/day effects and informative censoring or protocol failures will be handled. Fourth, define the coarsening-rate window carefully: estimating it only before detected onset can induce selection or unequal observation intervals, so use a prespecified common pre-onset rule and sensitivity analyses. Finally, the drive-only control is useful but cannot establish whether drive modifies the coupling effect; the design correctly avoids that claim. The study is also appropriately limited to this array and tested parameter range.

Rating (1-5): 4
